title: Latent cost surface and staffing switchboard (Q2 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet constructs a latent cost surface mapping small changes in token price and token volume to runway and headcount levers. Purpose: give GTM/finance a compact decisioning "switchboard" for when to pause hires, throttle burst capacity, or convert reserved capacity commitments under short price shocks. Draft for review with eng infra and SRE on cost elasticity assumptions.

Top-level assumptions (short):
- Base token price (hosted) = $0.015 per 1k tokens.
- Token forecast is per-feature aggregated across product lines; GPU cost is modeled as $0.60 per 1k tokens (all-in on hosted/spot mix) at current model mix.
- Hiring cost: $25k one-time ramp per new FTE; ongoing fully-burdened comp = $18k/mo.
- Other opex (support, infra infra ops, cloud egress) included as a flat % of revenue (15%).
- Currency: USD. Months are Apr 2026 -> Sep 2026 (6-month horizon).
- Sensitivity: evaluate 20% price up / 25% price down and a midshock case (-40% price for 6 weeks).

Interpretation notes:
- GPU cost is shown in $k (for the row: GPU Cost = cost-per-1k-tokens * (Forecast Tokens / 1k) i.e., $0.60 * token-k). We model GPU cost as largely fixed per token in the short-run.
- Net monthly burn delta is a simplified delta from revenue to operational burn including new hire ramp; higher burn in downside scenarios results from lower revenue while GPU spend remains roughly linear with token volume.
- Runway is an illustrative bucket assuming current cash cushion (not shown) divided by monthly burn; exact cash input omitted intentionally, see linked Confluence artifact.

Sensitivity matrix (summary):
- Price elasticity: each -10% price shock -> ~-10% revenue in near-term (linear assumption for hosted pass-through) -> runway loss approx 1.5 months per -10% given present cost mix.
- Token volume delta: each +10% token volume (same price) -> revenue +10% and GPU cost +10% -> marginal unit economics improve if price per token > GPU unit cost.

Hiring switchboard rules (operational triggers):
- Green: price change within +/-5% and token delta within +/-8% -> continue planned hiring cadence.
- Amber: price drop between -6% and -18% OR token drop > -12% -> freeze non-critical hiring, re-evaluate after 4 weeks, enable cost-saving burst throttles (reduce spot usage by 15%). Notify #finance and #sre.
- Red: price drop >= -18% OR sustained token drop >= -20% for two consecutive months -> immediate hiring freeze + pull forward reserved capacity reviews; accelerate quantization/quant-recompile projects. Engage execs and consider temporary SKU price increase for new signups.

Trigger matrix (concrete thresholds):
- If average token price realized < $0.011 (25% below base) for 2 weeks -> pause all non-customer-facing hires and hold contractor renewals.
- If token volume drops > 20% month-over-month and revenue impact > $1.5M/mo -> present contingency plan to CRO within 48h.

Cost-reduction playbook (mini):
1) Immediate: throttle burst capacity by capping transient GPUs (target 10-20% savings).
2) Short (2-6 weeks): pause hiring, reassign engineers from greenfield to quantization & inference optimization sprints.
3) Medium (1-3 months): renegotiate slab commitments and explore soft-commit rephasing with top three suppliers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate GPU cost per-1k assumptions with infra (ticket: JIRA-INF-4419).
- Add cash cushion row (requires CFO approval to include sensitive balance data).
- Cross-check model mix delta when prioritized quantization launches (expected 8-12% lower GPU cost).

Notes to self: get Priya and Diego's estimate on hiring ramp timing (M3 vs M6 productivity) and plug into the ramp curve column in the next revision. Also file a short-run executive one-pager if Amber triggers are reached.

Draft notes: leaving raw numbers (k) to keep sheet importable into the runway model. Expect to convert to a Google Sheet with formulas next round.
